title: 1950 AHSME Problem 30
statement: From a group of boys and girls, \(15\) girls leave. There are then left two boys for each girl. After this \(45\) boys leave. There are then \(5\) girls for each boy. The number of girls in the beginning was:

solutions.text:
Let the original counts be \(G\) girls and \(B\) boys. The two conditions give \[ \begin{aligned} B&=2(G-15),\\ G-15&=5(B-45). \end{aligned} \] Substituting the first into the second yields \[ \begin{aligned} G-15 &=5\bigl(2(G-15)-45\bigr)\\ &=10G-375. \end{aligned} \] Hence \(9G=360,\) so \(G=40.\)

Thus, the correct answer is A.
hints: Let \(G\) and \(B\) be the original numbers of girls and boys
Translate the two ratios as \(B=2(G-15)\) and \(G-15=5(B-45)\)
